title: Isolation and Quantification of Large Aging Neutrophil-Derived Vesicles
author: Hsu, Huang, et al.

steps.title: Prepare workspace and reagents
steps.instruction: Keep all samples, reagents and consumables on ice or at 4 °C unless otherwise stated; arrange all required equipment, buffers (sorting buffer, bronchoalveolar lavage buffer) and reagents (TruStain FcX, antibodies, counting beads) before starting.

steps.title: Isolate LAND‑V from mouse neutrophil culture
steps.instruction: Purify and quantify LAND‑V from 20 h in‑vitro cultured mouse neutrophils using sequential centrifugation, resuspension, antibody staining, washing, bead‑based counting and flow‑cytometric analysis.

substeps.instruction: Collect the cultured neutrophils (20 h) into a 50 mL sterile centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 min at 4 °C; gently collect the supernatant and discard the pellet. Repeat once to ensure removal of intact cells and large debris.
Centrifuge the pooled supernatant at 3 000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C, collect the pellet and resuspend in 20 mL PBS.
Centrifuge the suspension again at 3 000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the final pellet in 500 µL PBS for each 50 × 10⁶ starting neutrophils. Use immediately for functional assays or store on ice (4 °C) for ≤ 8 h (longer storage not recommended).
Aliquot 10 µL of the vesicle suspension into a 5 mL round‑bottom tube and add 100 µL sorting buffer (pre‑made, store ≤ 2 months at 4 °C).
Add 2 µL TruStain FcX, incubate 10 min on ice (4 °C) to block Fc receptors.
Add 1 µL BV421‑conjugated Ly6G (200 ng) and 1 µL APC‑conjugated CD42d (200 ng) without prior dilution; include a parallel tube with isotype controls. Incubate 15 min on ice in the dark.
Wash twice with 2 mL PBS by centrifuging 3 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C each wash; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the final pellet in 200 µL PBS and add 10 µL CountBright Plus Absolute Counting Beads.

Acquire samples on an Attune NxT flow cytometer within 2 h (no fixation). Use FSC 100, SSC 250, FSC threshold 2500, APC PMT gain 400, FITC PMT gain 350, BV421 PMT gain 350; keep flow rate < 10 000 events s⁻¹.

Apply the gating strategy (Figure 1B): exclude debris and cells by FSC‑A/SSC‑A, discard doublets (SSC‑A vs SSC‑H), select GFP⁺ (>90 %) particles (if GFP mice) or Ly6G⁺ particles, exclude CD42d⁺ platelet vesicles, and define LAND‑V as the GFP⁺/Ly6G⁺ population.
Quantify LAND‑V using: (collected LAND‑V count / collected bead count) × total beads added.

If ultra‑pure LAND‑V is required, sort the gated population using a ≥ 70 µm nozzle, the slowest feasible flow rate, aiming for ~2 000 LAND‑V s⁻¹ and droplet efficiency > 85 %. Include protease inhibitors in collection tubes and keep sorting at 4 °C.

steps.title: Identify LAND‑V in mouse peripheral blood
steps.instruction: Collect peripheral blood from MRP8‑Cre(+)/ROSA‑mTmG mice, isolate plasma‑derived vesicles by low‑speed centrifugation, stain (if needed) and analyze by flow cytometry.

substeps.instruction: Obtain blood via sub‑mandibular venipuncture using a 4–5 mm lancet; collect into a vacutainer containing EDTA or heparin. Optionally add extra EDTA to 2 mM final or heparin to 100 U mL⁻¹.
Transfer 400 µL anticoagulated blood into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge 300 × g for 5 min at room temperature (RT); collect supernatant into a 5 mL round‑bottom tube, discard pellet.
If supernatant remains red, repeat a 100 × g, 5 min, RT spin and transfer the clarified supernatant to a new tube (RBC lysis buffer must NOT be used).
Centrifuge the clarified supernatant at 3 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 300 µL PBS.

Perform flow cytometry within 2 h (no fixation). Use the gating strategy shown in Figure 2B: doublet exclusion, GFP⁺ particle selection, optional Ly6G/CD42d staining if mice lack GFP (see steps 22‑24).
If GFP is absent, repeat steps 15‑18, resuspend in 100 µL PBS, block Fc with TruStain FcX (2 µL), stain with Ly6G and CD42d (as in steps 6‑9), then follow the same gating (Figure 2C).
Discard doublets (SSC‑A vs SSC‑H), gate out CD42d⁺ platelet vesicles, and define Ly6G⁺ particles as LAND‑V.
Do NOT freeze LAND‑V; if storage is required, mix 1:1 with BamBanker Direct (Bulldog bio #BBD01) and store at –80 °C for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Identify and purify LAND‑V from bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF)
steps.instruction: Perform BAL, isolate vesicles by low‑speed centrifugation, stain for Ly6G/CD42d, and analyze or sort by flow cytometry.

substeps.instruction: Prepare cold bronchoalveolar lavage buffer (store ≤ 2 months at 4 °C).
Euthanize mouse (CO₂ chamber followed by cervical dislocation) and secure on a restrainer.
Make a vertical thoracic skin incision, open the rib cage without puncturing the lungs to expose trachea.
Insert a 24 G i.v. catheter ~1 cm into the trachea, tie a double surgeon’s knot with suture to secure, then remove the needle.

Load a 1 mL syringe with 800 µL cold lavage buffer; inject slowly, allowing lungs to inflate, then gently aspirate back. Repeat this injection/aspiration three times total (four lavages). Expected recovery ≈ 500–700 µL.
Collect the pooled lavage fluid into a 5 mL tube containing 3.0–3.2 mL cold lavage buffer.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at RT; collect supernatant and discard pellet (cells/debris).
Centrifuge the supernatant at 3 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant and resuspend pellet in 100 µL PBS.
Block Fc receptors with TruStain FcX (2 µL) and stain with Ly6G and CD42d antibodies (as in steps 6‑9), including isotype controls; incubate 15 min on ice in the dark.
Wash twice with 2 mL sorting buffer (3 000 × g, 5 min, 4 °C each).
Resuspend in 200 µL PBS, add 10 µL CountBright Plus beads, and acquire on flow cytometer within 2 h.
Apply gating (Figure 3I): doublet exclusion (SSC‑A vs SSC‑H), select Ly6G⁺ particles, exclude CD42d⁺ platelet vesicles, and define the remaining Ly6G⁺ events as BALF LAND‑V.
For downstream sorting, use the same gating; optimize sort conditions to maximize yield.

steps.title: Identify and quantify LAND‑V from human plasma
steps.instruction: Collect human blood, isolate plasma vesicles by sequential centrifugation, stain with anti‑human CD41/CD66b, and quantify by flow cytometry.

substeps.instruction: Draw 1 mL venous blood into a vacutainer containing EDTA or heparin.
Spin whole blood at 300 × g for 5 min at RT; carefully transfer 400 µL plasma to a new 5 mL tube without disturbing the cell pellet. If plasma remains red, repeat this spin.
Centrifuge plasma at 3 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the resulting pellet in 100 µL sorting buffer.
Add 2 µL human FcR blocking reagent; incubate 10 min on ice (4 °C).
Add 2 µL anti‑human CD41 (400 ng) and 2 µL anti‑human CD66b (400 ng) without dilution; include isotype‑control tube. Incubate 15 min on ice in the dark.
Wash twice with 2 mL sorting buffer by centrifuging 3 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C each wash; discard supernatant.
Resuspend final pellet in 200 µL PBS and add 10 µL CountBright Plus Absolute Counting Beads.

Acquire samples on flow cytometer within 2 h (no fixation). Use the gating strategy described in Figure 1B/2B: exclude debris, discard doublets, gate out CD41⁺ platelet EVs, and define CD66b⁺ events as human LAND‑V.
Calculate LAND‑V concentration using the same formula as step 13: (LAND‑V count / bead count) × total beads added.

description: To maximize experimental success, it is essential to maintain all samples, reagents, and materials on ice or at 4°C unless otherwise specified. Additionally, ensure that all necessary reagents, equipment, and workstations are prearranged and ready before initiating the protocol.
